Explain the example for keep component styles local

blocks.text: A CSS module gives a component named classes that are scoped by the build. It helps avoid collisions with another component's class names.

Use a Next.js App Router project. Save files at the paths shown. For these static examples, use output: "export" in next.config.ts and npm run build. They need Next.js tools and do not run in this playground.

blocks.title: Keep component styles local

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: The actual CSS file defines `.card`; importing it creates a styles mapping.
`styles.card` supplies the generated class name, so another module can also have a card name without a collision.

blocks.text: After saving the actual CSS rule in Card.module.css, the card gets a border and padding.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: The CSS comment here labels a separate file. Put real CSS, without the comment markers, in that file.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the card border colour in the module.
